docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
1. Write your analysis in Markdown → save to input_reports/report-name-DDmonYYYY.md

2. Add YAML frontmatter at the top of the file:

---
title: "Market Sage — Stock Action Plan"
date: 2026-06-09
category: action-plan
tags: [indian-equities, portfolio, zerodha]
description: "Phased deployment plan for ₹5L fresh capital across 7 new positions."
tickers: [COFORGE, NAVINFLUOR, CAMS, LALPATHLAB]
---

3. Run /generate-report-index — copies the report to docs/reports/, updates this index page, and rebuilds the site nav.

4. git add -A && git commit -m "add report" && git push — GitHub Actions deploys to gh-pages automatically.

docs.title: Large-Cap Avoidance Rule
docs.text: No new individual large-cap stocks, as the user's ₹5–5.5L in Nifty 50, Nifty Next 50, and large-cap MFs already provides top-100 market coverage. docs.title: LIC Shareholding Policy
docs.text: Per explicit analytical policy: LIC (Life Insurance Corporation of India) shareholding is not cited or used as a governance signal. LIC investments are subject to political direction rather than independent investment merit (evidence: Adani 2023 crisis purchases, ITC tobacco, Rajesh Exports). Only private domestic institutional holdings (SBI MF, HDFC MF, Kotak MF, ICICI Pru MF, Axis MF, Nippon MF etc.) are treated as genuine institutional validation.

docs.title: DII Decomposition Rule
docs.text: When DII % appears high in any shareholding pattern analysis, it is decomposed into "LIC" vs "Other private DIIs." Only private MFs and insurance companies (not LIC) are counted as positive governance signals.
